I'm trying to determine whether I would be able to see the Moon right now.

I'm in Lagos, Nigeria at 2026-04-09 09:40 WAT (UTC+0100) (2026-04-09T08:40:00Z in UTC), at latitude 6.5244 degrees and longitude 3.3792 degrees. My astronomy app says the Sun's altitude is 43.368 degrees and its azimuth is 85.647 degrees, so it is above the horizon. It says the Moon's altitude is 30.621 degrees and its azimuth is 232.237 degrees, so it is above the horizon. The Moon is 58.18 percent illuminated, 99.256 degrees from the Sun, and 399264.3 kilometers away. The sky brightness is bright daylight, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Yes—under those conditions, you would very likely be able to see the Moon with unaided eyes.

- It is **30.6° above the horizon**, comfortably high enough to avoid most horizon haze and obstructions.
- It is **58% illuminated**, so it should be a prominent half-to-gibbous Moon rather than a thin, difficult crescent.
- It is **99° from the Sun**, well separated from the Sun’s glare.
- The Sun is at azimuth **85.6°** (roughly east), while the Moon is at **232.2°** (roughly southwest), so they are in very different parts of the sky.
- In bright daylight the Moon can look washed out, but its angular size and brightness are ample for naked-eye detection when you know where to look.

From Lagos, look **southwest**, about **31° above the horizon**—roughly one-third of the way from the horizon to overhead. It may appear pale against the blue sky, so shielding your eyes from direct sunlight and using a building or your hand to block glare can help. Avoid looking anywhere near the Sun itself.
